rationale: Attempt-00 passed numerical checks, compiled, and simulated at 234.82 us with block_M=128, block_N=64, block_K=64, num_stages=1, swizzle=0; actual smem hit exactly 32768 bytes with 122 registers and 3 blocks/SM. Only one point exists, so exclusion is minimal and no domain widening is needed. Since the baseline row-major point is already evaluated, I now open swizzle to [0,4,8,16] to test the serpentine-panel locality hypothesis, keeping allowed M/N/K tiles (M=N=K=2048 divisible by all). Cap stays at the hard 32768 portability limit; large tile/stage combinations exceeding the estimator will be filtered by HiGHS's byte constraint, with compiled smem still checked. Weights shift modestly: raise traffic to 1.5 to probe whether swizzle-driven reuse reduces simulated DRAM traffic, lower footprint to 0.75 since attempt-00 already saturates the cap and heavy footprint pressure could bias away from good pipelines, and keep launches/pipeline at 1 to avoid overfitting to a single sample. The panel reuse feature remains an analytic hypothesis; I will compare simulated DRAM/latency across swizzle values before trusting it. Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR; CUDA binary is not executed, and GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. This is exploratory and not a claim of global optimality.
